sources: Joint ranges: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons, Joint Motion (1965), as tabulated at https://goniometer.io/range-of-motion; trunk from WikEM https://wikem.org/wiki/Joint_ROM_(Table); shin rotation at 90 degrees of knee flexion from https://jeo-esska.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s40634-018-0141-9/tables/2; shin rotation needs the knee bent, as the straight knee locks (screw-home mechanism): https://www.physio-pedia.com/Screw_Home_Mechanism
Muscle actions: Kenhub https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy-en/ and TeachMeAnatomy https://teachmeanatomy.info/, checked against each part's flow text in src/data/muscular.json

Two-joint stretch positions: ExRx https://exrx.net/Lists/Directory and learnmuscles https://learnmuscles.com/; figure-4 piriformis stretch is hip flexion, adduction and external rotation (Park, Shim and Chung 2017, J Phys Ther Sci 29(10):1811): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5684014/
Hold times: ACSM (Garber et al. 2011), via Page 2012 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3273886/; jaw: Rocabado 6x6 https://en.irct.ir/trial/76578

Nerve glides: sliders vs tensioners, Coppieters & Butler 2008 https://research.vu.nl/en/publications/do-sliders-slide-and-tensioners-tension-an-analysis-of-neurodynam/; review, Basson 2017 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28704626/; upper-limb sequences, Physiotutors https://www.physiotutors.com/wiki/upper-limb-nerve-sliders-tensioners/; slump, Physiotutors https://www.physiotutors.com/wiki/slump-test/; sciatic excursion with knee and neck extension, Ellis 2012 https://research.bond.edu.au/en/publications/comparison-of-longitudinal-sciatic-nerve-movement-with-different-/; side-lying femoral glider as practitioners teach it https://theprehabguys.com/vimeo-video/side-lying-femoral-nerve-glider-2/

Joint-only moves: ankle mobilisation with movement, Vicenzino 2006 https://search.pedro.org.au/search-results/record-detail/16142 (review https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4483387); hip self-mobilisation evidence level 5, Reiman & Matheson 2013 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3811738/; cat-camel, McGill https://www.unm.edu/~lkravitz/Article%20folder/lowbackstability.html; CARs, no outcomes published https://ichgcp.net/clinical-trials-registry/NCT03456050

Foam rolling: Wiewelhove 2019 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31024339/; Wilke 2020 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7919347; Konrad 2022 https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9474417/; mechanism, Behm & Wilke 2019 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31256353/; fascia needs supra-physiological force to deform, Chaudhry 2008 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18723456/; contraindications Delphi https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8622134/

head.name: Head on the neck (top two neck joints)

finger-joints.name: Middle and end finger joints (PIP and DIP)

subtalar.name: Below the ankle (sole in and out)

stretches.name: Chin-tuck nod
stretches.how: Sit tall. Glide the chin straight back, then nod it down as if making a double chin.
stretches.cue: Feel it at the base of the skull.

variants.label: nod chin in, then down

stretches.name: Neck flexion (chin to chest)
stretches.how: Let the chin drop toward the chest; let the upper back round slightly.
stretches.cue: Hands can rest on the back of the head; no pulling.

variants.label: chin to chest

stretches.name: Upper-trapezius stretch
stretches.how: Sit on one hand to hold the shoulder down. Tip the opposite ear toward the opposite shoulder, chin slightly down.

variants.label: ear away, nose slightly toward stretched side

stretches.name: Levator scapulae stretch
stretches.how: Turn the head 45 degrees away and look down toward that armpit. Rest the same-side hand on the back of the head (elbow up).

variants.label: nose toward opposite armpit, hand behind head

stretches.name: Scalene stretch
stretches.how: Hold the collarbone down with the opposite hand, breathe out, then tip the head away.
stretches.cue: Stop if the arm tingles: that is the brachial plexus, not muscle.

variants.label: ear away, chin up and away (front scalene)
ear away, chin level (middle scalene)
ear away, chin toward opposite shoulder (back scalene)

stretches.name: Sternocleidomastoid stretch
stretches.how: Hold the collarbone down. Tip the head away, turn the face toward the stretched side, then tilt the head back while keeping a slight chin tuck.
stretches.cue: Small range; move slowly.

variants.label: ear away, turn toward, look up

stretches.name: Neck extension, mouth closed (front of neck)
stretches.how: Sit tall, close the lips and press the tongue to the roof of the mouth, then look up to the ceiling.
stretches.cue: Keep the jaw closed: that lengthens the muscles under the chin as well.

variants.label: look up, lips closed, tongue on palate

stretches.name: Neck rotation
stretches.how: Turn the head as far as is comfortable to the left, then to the right.

variants.label: turn the head to the left
turn the head to the right

stretches.name: Neck side-bend
stretches.how: Tip one ear toward the shoulder without turning the face.

variants.label: ear toward the opposite shoulder

stretches.name: Controlled jaw opening
stretches.how: Rest the tongue on the roof of the mouth and open as far as you can without it leaving; then open fully.
stretches.cue: No clicking or pain; small range is fine.

variants.label: hinge open with tongue on palate, then open fully (the jaw slides forward)

stretches.name: Jaw retrusion
stretches.how: Teeth slightly apart, gently draw the jaw straight back.

variants.label: teeth slightly apart, jaw drawn straight back

stretches.name: Side-to-side jaw glide
stretches.how: Teeth slightly apart (a pencil between the front teeth helps); slide the jaw to the left, then to the right.

variants.label: jaw slides to the left
jaw slides to the right

stretches.name: Tongue range
stretches.how: Stick the tongue out and up toward the nose; then curl it back along the roof of the mouth.
stretches.cue: Lengthens the tongue muscles; not a proven stretch.

variants.label: tongue out and up
tongue curled back

stretches.name: Surprise face
stretches.how: Raise the eyebrows high and open the eyes wide.
stretches.cue: Lengthens these muscles by making the opposite expression; there is no evidence it changes them.

variants.label: surprise face

stretches.name: Frown
stretches.how: Draw the eyebrows down.
stretches.cue: Lengthens these muscles by making the opposite expression; there is no evidence it changes them.

variants.label: frown

stretches.name: Pucker (long "O")
stretches.how: Push the lips forward into a long O, drawing the mouth corners in.
stretches.cue: Lengthens these muscles by making the opposite expression; there is no evidence it changes them.

variants.label: pucker (long "o")

stretches.name: Wide smile, mouth open
stretches.how: Smile as wide as you can with the lips apart, then open the mouth.
stretches.cue: Lengthens these muscles by making the opposite expression; there is no evidence it changes them.

variants.label: wide smile, mouth open

stretches.name: Lower-lip moves (pout, then show the bottom teeth)
stretches.how: Push the lower lip up and out, then pull it down to show the bottom teeth.
stretches.cue: Lengthens these muscles by making the opposite expression; there is no evidence it changes them.

variants.label: lower-lip moves (pout, then show the bottom teeth)

stretches.name: Nose and cheeks (flare, sniff, puff)
stretches.how: Flare the nostrils, then sniff them narrow; puff the cheeks with air.
stretches.cue: Lengthens these muscles by making the opposite expression; there is no evidence it changes them.

variants.label: nose and cheeks (flare, sniff, puff)

stretches.name: Eye range (look to the eight end points)
stretches.how: Keep the head still and move only the eyes to each end point.
stretches.cue: Lengthens each eye muscle by looking the opposite way; this is range of motion, not a stretch with any known benefit.

variants.label: look up
look down
look right
look left
look down and to the right
look up and to the right
look down and to the left
look up and to the left
close the eyes gently

stretches.name: Child's pose / rounded back (spinal flexion)
stretches.how: Kneel, sit back toward the heels and walk the hands forward, letting the whole back round.
stretches.cue: Breathe into the back of the ribs.

variants.label: sit back on heels, arms forward, back rounded

stretches.name: Prone press-up (spinal extension)
stretches.how: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders; press the chest up, letting the hips and belly stay down. Breathe in.
stretches.cue: Stop if pain travels down a leg.

variants.label: lying face down, press the chest up, hips down

stretches.name: Standing side-bend, arm overhead (breathe out)
stretches.how: Stand, raise one arm and reach up and over to the other side; breathe out fully at the end.
stretches.cue: Lengthens the diaphragm and intercostals on the open side as well.

variants.label: reach up and over to the other side, breathe out

stretches.name: Seated or lying trunk twist
stretches.how: Sit tall (or lie with knees bent and let them fall to one side) and turn the chest to the left, then to the right.

variants.label: turn the chest to the left
turn the chest to the right

stretches.name: Full breath out
stretches.how: Breathe out slowly and completely, letting the ribs sink and the belly draw in.
stretches.cue: Lengthens the breathing-in muscles; not a proven stretch.

variants.label: empty the lungs fully, ribs down

stretches.name: Full breath in
stretches.how: Breathe in as fully as you can, letting the ribs widen and the belly relax outward.
stretches.cue: Lengthens the breathing-out muscles; not a proven stretch.

variants.label: fill the lungs fully, ribs up and out, belly out

stretches.name: Deep squat with belly breathing (pelvic floor)
stretches.how: Sink into a supported deep squat (or happy baby). On each breath in, let the pelvic floor relax and drop; do not push or strain.
stretches.cue: Pain, urgency or heaviness: see a pelvic-health physio.

variants.label: deep squat, breathe in and let the pelvic floor drop
happy baby (on your back, knees to armpits)

stretches.name: Doorway chest stretch
stretches.how: Forearm on a door frame, step through until the front of the shoulder and chest stretch. Change the arm height to move the stretch.
stretches.cue: Keep the shoulder blade drawn back, not the arm bone pushed forward.

variants.label: elbow below shoulder (about 60 degrees)
elbow at shoulder height (90 degrees)
elbow above shoulder (about 135 degrees)

stretches.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
stretches.how: Bring one arm across the chest and hold it above the elbow with the other hand.
stretches.cue: Keep the shoulder blade flat (not hitched up).

variants.label: arm across the chest

stretches.name: Overhead lat stretch
stretches.how: Kneel with the elbows on a bench (palms together, elbows bent) and sit the hips back; or hang from a bar.
stretches.cue: Bending the elbows adds the long head of triceps.

variants.label: arms overhead, palms up, sit hips back and side-bend away

stretches.name: Shoulder internal-rotation stretch (sleeper)
stretches.how: Lie on the side with the bottom arm forward at shoulder height, elbow bent; gently press the forearm down.
stretches.cue: Gentle: it loads the back of the joint capsule too.

variants.label: lying on the side, forearm lowered toward the floor

stretches.name: Shoulder external-rotation stretch
stretches.how: Elbow at the side and bent 90 degrees; turn the forearm outward against a door frame or with a stick.

variants.label: elbow at the side, forearm turned out (stick or door frame)

stretches.name: Hands clasped behind the back
stretches.how: Clasp the hands behind you with straight elbows and lift them away from the back.
stretches.cue: Turning the palms down adds biceps.

variants.label: arms straight behind, palms down, lift

stretches.name: Towel behind the back (shoulder adduction + internal rotation)
stretches.how: Hold a towel behind the back; the top hand gently pulls the bottom hand up the spine.

variants.label: hand up the back

stretches.name: Upper-back round (shoulder blades apart)
stretches.how: Wrap the arms around yourself (or hold a post) and round the upper back, letting the shoulder blades slide apart.

variants.label: hug yourself, shoulders down, upper back rounded
reach across toward the opposite hip, shoulder shrugged

stretches.name: Shoulder-blade squeeze down and back
stretches.how: Put the back of the hand on the lower back and draw the shoulder blade back and toward the spine.

variants.label: hand behind back, blade squeezed down and in

stretches.name: Shoulder shrug back (collarbone up)
stretches.how: Shrug the shoulders up and back and breathe in.
stretches.cue: A gentle range move for subclavius and the lower trapezius.

variants.label: shrug up and back, breathe in

stretches.name: Biceps wall stretch
stretches.how: Place the hand on a wall behind you at shoulder height, thumb down, and turn the body away.

variants.label: hand on wall behind, thumb down, turn away

stretches.name: Overhead triceps stretch
stretches.how: Raise the arm, bend the elbow so the hand drops behind the head, and ease the elbow back with the other hand.

variants.label: elbow up, hand down the back

stretches.name: Forearm rotation end range
stretches.how: With the elbow straight, turn the palm up as far as it goes; then turn it down. The other hand can help at the wrist.

variants.label: palm fully up, elbow straight
palm fully down, elbow straight

stretches.name: Wrist and finger flexor stretch
stretches.how: Arm straight in front, palm up; with the other hand pull the fingers (and thumb) back.
stretches.cue: Tipping the hand to each side shifts the stretch between the wrist flexors.

variants.label: elbow straight, palm up, wrist and fingers back
same, hand tipped toward the little finger
same, hand tipped toward the thumb

stretches.name: Wrist and finger extensor stretch
stretches.how: Arm straight in front, palm down; make a loose fist and bend the wrist down with the other hand.
stretches.cue: Thumb-tucked variant (b) is gentle only: it is also the De Quervain test position.

variants.label: elbow straight, palm down, fist curled, wrist down
same, hand tipped toward the little finger, thumb tucked
same, hand tipped toward the thumb

stretches.name: Hand intrinsic stretch (hook fist)
stretches.how: Keep the big knuckles straight and bend the middle and end finger joints (a hook); press gently on the bent fingers.

variants.label: knuckles straight, finger joints bent

stretches.name: Finger spread and squeeze
stretches.how: Palm flat on a table, spread the fingers as wide as they go; then press them together and cross them.

variants.label: spread the fingers wide (palm on table)
squeeze the fingers together and cross them

stretches.name: Thumb web-space stretch
stretches.how: Use the other hand to ease the thumb away from the index finger, opening the web space.

variants.label: thumb pulled away from the index finger

stretches.name: Flat palm, thumb and little finger back
stretches.how: Press the palm flat on a table and ease the thumb and little finger back and out of the palm.

variants.label: palm flattened, thumb back and little finger back

stretches.name: Hamstring stretch (straight-leg raise)
stretches.how: Lie on the back and raise one straight leg with a strap until the back of the thigh stretches.
stretches.cue: Keep the knee straight and the pelvis down; ankle relaxed (pulling the toes up adds the sciatic nerve: see the sciatic glide).

variants.label: lying on the back, straight leg raised (strap)
same, leg across the midline, foot turned in
same, leg out to the side, foot turned out

stretches.name: Standing quad stretch
stretches.how: Stand on one leg (hold something) and draw the heel toward the buttock, knees together.
stretches.cue: Tuck the pelvis under to add rectus femoris.

variants.label: heel toward buttock, knee pointing down

stretches.name: Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch
stretches.how: Kneel on one knee, tuck the pelvis under and shift forward until the front of the back hip stretches.
stretches.cue: Do not arch the low back.

variants.label: back knee down, tuck pelvis, shift forward
same, arm up and side-bend away
same, back heel pulled up (couch stretch)
same, back knee out to the side (thigh in)

stretches.name: Butterfly / wide-leg adductor stretch
stretches.how: Sit with the soles together and let the knees fall; then sit with straight legs wide apart and lean forward.

variants.label: soles together, knees down (butterfly)
legs wide, knees straight (straddle)
side lunge, straight leg turned up

stretches.name: Figure-4 / pigeon
stretches.how: Lie on the back, cross one ankle over the other knee and pull the bottom thigh toward the opposite shoulder.

variants.label: ankle on the other knee, thigh pulled toward the opposite shoulder

stretches.name: Knee to opposite shoulder
stretches.how: Lie on the back and pull one bent knee toward the opposite shoulder.

variants.label: bent knee pulled toward the opposite shoulder

stretches.name: Hip internal-rotation stretch
stretches.how: Lie on the back with the feet wide and let both knees drop in toward each other.

variants.label: lying, knees bent wide, let both knees fall inward
lying face down, thigh slightly out, knee bent, foot falls outward

stretches.name: Standing cross-behind (outer hip)
stretches.how: Cross the stretched leg behind the other and push that hip out to the side, leaning the trunk away.

variants.label: stretched leg crossed behind, hip pushed out

stretches.name: Shin rotation, knee bent
stretches.how: Sit with the knee bent to 90 degrees and the thigh still; turn the foot and shin out, or in, as far as they go.
stretches.cue: The shin only turns while the knee is bent; with the knee straight the turn comes from the hip.

variants.label: knee bent, foot and shin turned out
knee bent, foot and shin turned in

stretches.name: Calf stretch, back knee straight
stretches.how: Hands on a wall, step one foot back, keep that knee straight and press the heel down.
stretches.cue: Point the back foot straight ahead.

variants.label: lunge at a wall, back knee straight, heel down

stretches.name: Calf stretch, back knee bent
stretches.how: From C1, bend the back knee while keeping the heel down; the stretch moves low in the calf.

variants.label: same, back knee bent

stretches.name: Toes-up calf and sole stretch
stretches.how: Put the ball of the foot and toes up against a wall with the heel on the floor; lean in. Then pull the big toe up and out with your hand.

variants.label: toes up against the wall, knee straight
big toe pulled up and out, arch flattened

stretches.name: Shin stretch (top of the foot)
stretches.how: Kneel and sit back on the tops of the feet, or stand and rest the top of the curled toes on the floor behind you.

variants.label: foot pointed, toes curled, sole turned out
foot pointed, toes curled, sole turned in

stretches.name: Ankle roll-in and roll-out
stretches.how: Seated, hold the foot and turn the sole inward, then outward, with the foot pulled up.

variants.label: sole turned in, foot up (outer ankle)
sole turned out, foot up (inner ankle)

stretches.name: Toe spread and squeeze
stretches.how: Lace the fingers between the toes and spread them; then squeeze the toes together.

variants.label: fingers laced between the toes, toes spread
toes squeezed together

stretches.name: Inferior shoulder glide
stretches.how: Sit side-on to a table with the forearm resting on it and the arm out at about 60 degrees. Let the shoulder sink down away from the ear, then lean the body gently toward the table so the top of the arm bone glides down in its socket.
stretches.cue: Keep the neck and shoulder relaxed; it should feel like easing, not stretching.
stretches.evidence: Used in rehab for a stiff (frozen) shoulder, where joint mobilisation helps; there is no evidence it does anything for a shoulder that already moves freely.

variants.label: arm resting out on a table, shoulder sinking down

stretches.name: Thoracic extension over a roller
stretches.how: Lie on the back with a foam roller across the upper back, hands behind the head and hips on the floor. Breathe out and let the upper back arch over the roller, then roll it one hand-width up or down and repeat.
stretches.cue: Keep the ribs down and the low back still; the bend should come from the upper back.
stretches.hold: 3 slow breaths at each of 3 levels
stretches.evidence: Little research of its own; it is safe and reaches the stiff upper back, which most stretches skip.

joints: radiate ligament of head of rib

variants.label: upper back arched over the roller, hands behind the head

stretches.name: Open-book thoracic rotation
stretches.how: Lie on one side with the hips and knees bent to a right angle and the arms straight out in front, palms together. Keeping the knees together, open the top arm across and turn the upper back toward the ceiling, then close it again.
stretches.cue: The knees stay stacked so the low back stays put; follow the hand with the eyes.
stretches.evidence: Taught widely to turn the upper back while the low back stays locked; instructional sources only, no trials.

joints: radiate ligament of head of rib

variants.label: lying on the other side, the top arm and chest turned open

stretches.name: Cat-camel
stretches.how: On hands and knees, slowly round the whole back up toward the ceiling with the head down, then let it sag gently with the head up. About 6 slow cycles.
stretches.cue: Move gently through the middle of the range; this eases the spine rather than stretching it.
stretches.evidence: Recommended by McGill to move the spine through its range before exercise; expert advice, no trials of its own.

variants.label: cat: back rounded up, head down
camel: back sagging, head up

stretches.name: Hip long-axis distraction (band)
stretches.how: Lie on the back with a long band looped around the ankle and tied to something solid past the feet. Slide away until the band gently pulls the leg long, then relax the leg and let it draw the hip joint apart.
stretches.cue: Let the leg go heavy; ease off if anything pinches in the groin.
stretches.evidence: Expert opinion only: reviews rate hip self-mobilisation evidence level 5, with no direct trials (Reiman & Matheson 2013).

variants.label: leg slightly bent, out and turned out (the hip's loosest position), band pulling it long

stretches.name: Hip rock-back (posterior glide)
stretches.how: On hands and knees, rock the hips slowly back toward the heels and forward again. A band looped around the top of one thigh and pulling backward adds a glide to that hip.
stretches.cue: Keep the back long; stop the rock before the low back rounds.
stretches.evidence: Expert opinion only: reviews rate hip self-mobilisation evidence level 5, with no direct trials (Reiman & Matheson 2013).

variants.label: hips rocked back toward the heels

stretches.name: Ankle glide with knee-to-wall (mobilisation with movement)
stretches.how: Half-kneel facing a wall with the front foot a hand-width from it. Loop a band low around the front of the ankle, anchored behind you, so it pulls the ankle bone back. Keeping the heel down, drive the knee forward over the middle toes toward the wall, then back.
stretches.cue: The heel stays down and the knee tracks over the second toe.
stretches.evidence: Moderate: it increased ankle bending in people with stiff ankles after a sprain (Vicenzino 2006, PEDro 7/10).

variants.label: knee driven forward over the toes, heel down

stretches.name: Controlled joint circles (CARs)
stretches.how: Keeping the rest of the body still, move one joint around the biggest, slowest circle it allows, then the other way. The model shows one point on the circle.
stretches.cue: Slow and controlled; the circle shrinks wherever the joint is stiff.
stretches.evidence: From Functional Range Conditioning; no published outcomes (expert opinion only).

variants.label: shoulder: arm circled up, back and around
hip: standing on one leg, the bent knee circled out

stretches.name: Median nerve glide
stretches.how: Hold the arm out to the side at shoulder height, palm up. Bend the wrist and fingers back while tipping the head toward that shoulder; then let the wrist bend down as the head comes back up.
stretches.cue: Move smoothly in and out, 10 times; never hold. Stop if tingling or numbness builds or lingers.
stretches.evidence: A slider moved the median nerve about twice as far as a tensioner at about an eighth of the strain (Coppieters & Butler 2008). Evidence that nerve glides relieve symptoms is limited and mixed (Basson 2017).

nervous: common palmar digital branches of median nerve
proper palmar digital branches of median nerve

variants.label: slider: wrist back as the head tips toward the arm
tensioner, only if the slider feels easy: wrist back as the head tips away

stretches.name: Ulnar nerve glide
stretches.how: Hold the arm out to the side, palm down. Bend the elbow and the wrist back to bring the hand toward the ear, like a mask over the eye, while tipping the head toward the hand; then straighten as the head comes back up.
stretches.cue: Move smoothly in and out, 10 times; never hold. Stop if tingling or numbness builds or lingers.
stretches.evidence: A slider moved the median nerve about twice as far as a tensioner at about an eighth of the strain (Coppieters & Butler 2008). Evidence that nerve glides relieve symptoms is limited and mixed (Basson 2017).

variants.label: slider: hand to the ear as the head tips toward it
tensioner, only if the slider feels easy: hand to the ear as the head tips away

stretches.name: Radial nerve glide
stretches.how: Let the arm hang a little away from the side, turned in with the palm facing back. Drop the shoulder and bend the wrist and fingers down while tipping the head toward that shoulder; then release the wrist as the head comes back up.
stretches.cue: Move smoothly in and out, 10 times; never hold. Stop if tingling or numbness builds or lingers.
stretches.evidence: A slider moved the median nerve about twice as far as a tensioner at about an eighth of the strain (Coppieters & Butler 2008). Evidence that nerve glides relieve symptoms is limited and mixed (Basson 2017).

nervous: dorsal digital branches of radial nerve

variants.label: slider: wrist bent down as the head tips toward the arm
tensioner, only if the slider feels easy: wrist bent down as the head tips away

stretches.name: Sciatic nerve glide (seated slump)
stretches.how: Sit on the edge of a chair, slumped slightly. Straighten one knee while looking up; then bend the knee back down as the chin drops.
stretches.cue: Move smoothly in and out, 10 times; never hold. Stop if tingling or numbness builds or lingers.
stretches.evidence: A slider moved the median nerve about twice as far as a tensioner at about an eighth of the strain (Coppieters & Butler 2008). Evidence that nerve glides relieve symptoms is limited and mixed (Basson 2017). Straightening the knee while looking up moved the sciatic nerve furthest in an ultrasound study (Ellis 2012).

variants.label: slider: knee straightened while looking up
tensioner, only if the slider feels easy: knee straightened and toes pulled up with the chin down

stretches.name: Femoral nerve glide (side-lying)
stretches.how: Lie on the other side with the bottom knee drawn up. Bend the top knee, holding the foot (or a strap), and take the thigh slightly back while tipping the head back; then let the knee come forward as the head comes down.
stretches.cue: Move smoothly in and out, 10 times; never hold. Stop if tingling or numbness builds or lingers.
stretches.evidence: A slider moved the median nerve about twice as far as a tensioner at about an eighth of the strain (Coppieters & Butler 2008). Evidence that nerve glides relieve symptoms is limited and mixed (Basson 2017). There is no published protocol for a femoral slider: this one follows the slider principle as practitioners teach it.

nervous: anterior cutaneous branches of femoral nerve

variants.label: slider: knee bent and thigh back as the head tips back
tensioner, only if the slider feels easy: knee bent and thigh back with the chin down

stretches.name: Foam roll: calves
stretches.how: Sit with a roller under one calf and the hands behind you. Lift the hips and roll slowly from below the knee to above the ankle; cross the other leg on top for more pressure.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Foam roll: hamstrings
stretches.how: Sit with the roller under one thigh and the hands behind you; roll slowly from just above the knee to below the buttock.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Foam roll: quadriceps
stretches.how: Lie face down propped on the forearms with the roller under one thigh; roll slowly from above the knee to the hip.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Foam roll: outer thigh
stretches.how: Lie on one side propped on the forearm with the roller under the outside of the thigh, the top foot on the floor in front for support; roll between the hip and the knee.
stretches.cue: The iliotibial band itself is far too stiff to lengthen or loosen; rolling here works on the muscles beside it.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Foam roll: inner thigh
stretches.how: Lie face down with one knee out to the side and bent, the roller under the inner thigh; roll from above the knee toward the groin.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Ball roll: buttock
stretches.how: Sit on a massage ball under one buttock, that ankle crossed over the other knee; roll in small circles over the tender spots.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: ball under one buttock

stretches.name: Foam roll: upper back
stretches.how: Lie on the back with the roller across the upper back, arms crossed over the chest and hips lifted; roll slowly between the shoulder blades and the bottom of the ribs.
stretches.cue: Stay on the upper back; do not roll the low back or the neck.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Foam roll: side of the back (lats)
stretches.how: Lie on one side with the bottom arm overhead and the roller under the armpit; roll slowly down the side of the back to the bottom of the ribs.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Ball roll: chest
stretches.how: Stand facing a wall with a massage ball between the wall and the front of the shoulder, below the collarbone; lean in and roll slowly across the chest.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

variants.label: ball against a wall, under the collarbone

stretches.name: Roll: forearms
stretches.how: Kneel with the forearm resting on the roller, palm down, and roll from the wrist to the elbow; turn the palm up to roll the other side.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

muscular: humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris

variants.label: roll slowly along it

stretches.name: Ball roll: sole of the foot
stretches.how: Stand or sit with a ball under one foot and roll it slowly from the heel to the ball of the foot.
stretches.evidence: About 4% more range for a short time before exercise and a little less soreness after it (Wiewelhove 2019); no better than stretching for range (Wilke 2020).

diaphragm.note: Breathing out fully (with a side-bend) lengthens it; not a proven stretch.

brachioradialis.note: Brings the forearm to thumb-up from either end, so both rotations lengthen it a little.

extensor pollicis longus.note: It can also help draw the thumb in toward the index finger.

abductor digiti minimi of hand.note: Squeeze the little finger in, with the knuckle straight.

lumbar rotator.note: Mostly a position sensor; a twist lengthens it only slightly.

platysma.note: Pulls the mouth corners and lower lip down: smiling widely while looking up lengthens it.

digastric.note: Lengthened by closing the jaw and looking up, which draws the hyoid down; no source describes a stretch for it.

geniohyoid.note: Lengthened by closing the jaw and looking up, which draws the hyoid down; no source describes a stretch for it.

mylohyoid.note: Lengthened by closing the jaw and looking up, which draws the hyoid down; no source describes a stretch for it.

stylohyoid.note: Lengthened by closing the jaw and looking up, which draws the hyoid down; no source describes a stretch for it.

omohyoid.note: Looking up lengthens the front of the neck a little; no source describes a stretch for it.

sternohyoid.note: It also pulls the hyoid down. Extend the neck gently and slowly.

sternothyroid.note: Looking up lengthens the front of the neck a little; no source describes a stretch for it.

thyrohyoid.note: Looking up lengthens the front of the neck a little; no source describes a stretch for it.

superior head of lateral pterygoid.note: Steadies the disc; retrusion lengthens it.

temporoparietalis.note: Barely moves the scalp; frowning lengthens it slightly.

depressor septi nasi.note: Pulls the nose tip down (sources disagree whether it widens or narrows the nostril); the range is tiny.

common tendinous ring.cannot: A ring of tendon that anchors the four rectus muscles; it does not contract or lengthen.

transversus abdominis.note: Only compresses the belly; a full breath in with the belly relaxed lengthens it.

pyramidalis.note: Tenses the midline seam; trunk extension lengthens it slightly.

external anal sphincter.cannot: A ring-shaped sphincter: it can only relax (as in a reverse Kegel), not be stretched by a position; deliberate stretching is a clinical procedure.

gluteus medius.note: Front fibres turn the thigh in, back fibres turn it out.

piriformis.note: Turns the thigh out with the hip straight but in when it is bent past about 90 degrees, so it is stretched by turning in (hip straight) or out (hip bent).

calcaneal tendon.note: A tendon, lengthened with the calf muscles.

first lumbrical of foot.note: Toes pulled up at the base, then curled at the tips.

second lumbrical of foot.note: Toes pulled up at the base, then curled at the tips.

third lumbrical of foot.note: Toes pulled up at the base, then curled at the tips.

fourth lumbrical of foot.note: Toes pulled up at the base, then curled at the tips.
